title: Lord, What Is Man, Poor Feeble Man
description: Lord, What Is Man, Poor Feeble Man in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 144, part 2, headed “The vanity of man, and condescension of God”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, what is man, poor fee-ble man, Born of the earth at first! His life a sha-dow, light and vain, Still hast-ing to the dust.

lines: Lord, what is man, poor feeble man,
Born of the earth at first!
His life a shadow, light and vain,
O what is feeble dying man
That God should make it his concern
That God who darts his lightnings down,
And mountains tremble at his frown,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
